newsitem.title: INDIA: Mass detentions start before Miss World's big night.
newsitem.headline: Mass detentions start before Miss World's big night.

text.p: Bangalore police rounded-up militant activists on Friday ahead of the Miss World pageant, while a firebrand protest leader promising self-immolation if the show goes ahead went into hiding.
An ally of the leader of a women's group whose members said they would burn themselves alive in protest said Kinay Narayana Shashikala was trying to stay out of police clutches.
"She's not going to surface because the police will catch her. I'm in contact with her," Pramila Nesargi, a right-wing Hindu nationalist Karnataka state deputy, said.

Police Commissioner S.C. Burman said 35 people were detained in the morning to head off trouble and the figure could reach between 150 and 200 by Friday evening, with 24 hours still to go before Miss World's big night.

Nesargi, a lawyer, and Shashikala, a law student, have been at the forefront of various factions hoping to block or spoil the three hour extravaganza on Saturday night. Shashikala has said 15 members of the traditionalist Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) will join the 20,000 audience at Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, where Miss World is to be crowned, to carry out their threat of self-immolation.
"They're very firm about going ahead with the plan," Nesargi said.
The annual international event is expected to draw a television audience of two billion in 115 countries, but local protesters say it offends Indian culture and demeans women.
More than 10,000 security officers, including elite commandos, were expected to be on patrol on Saturday. They will be joined by regular army soldiers following a court ruling in New Delhi.
The Supreme Court overturned an earlier court ruling that government soldiers could not be used to safeguard the event.

"Our first job is to save lives. We do not want anything to happen to them (the suicide squad). Because if anything happens it will give rise to mass hysteria not just in the state but across the country," Burman told Reuters.
Burman said earlier his officers were tailing Shashikala.
The police chief had no comment on a threat by a group calling itself the Indian Tigers that 400 activists would infiltrate the crowd and carry out lightning attacks inside and outside the stadium.

The Indian Tigers were unheard of until a few weeks ago when they attacked the Bangalore offices of the pageant's organisers, the Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd (ABCL), and claimed responsibility for a couple of small bomb blasts that injured no one.
"We are prepared for every eventuality," Burman said.
The state government has ordered schools and colleges to close on Friday and Saturday.

Banks and government offices were open, but the Hindu nationalist opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has called for a protest strike that was expected to mean transport stoppages and shop closures in some parts of the city.
"The BJP has made it a political issue. They are desperate and lost sight of what has to be done," Karnataka chief minister J.H. Patel said.
Meanwhile, the 88 contestants rested following their dress rehearsal on Thursday.
The Supreme Court provided some good news for drinkers among the audience. Alcohol can now be served. Miss World, if all goes well, will be toasted in champagne.
